questions.text: उत्प्रेरक परिवर्तित करते हैं :
questions.text_english: The role of a catalyst is to change :
questions.solution: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower energy barrier, thereby increasing the rate of reaction. It does not change the equilibrium constant (A), as it speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally. It does not alter the enthalpy (B) or Gibbs energy (C) of the reaction, since these are thermodynamic state functions dependent only on the initial and final states. Therefore, the correct answer is (D).
questions.topic: Activation Energy and Catalysis

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अणुओं में से किसकी प्रकृति किरेल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following molecules is chiral in nature ?
questions.solution: A chiral molecule has a carbon atom bonded to four different groups (an asymmetric carbon centre). In 2-chlorobutane (CH3CHClCH2CH3), the carbon bearing the chlorine is bonded to H, Cl, CH3, and CH2CH3 — all four groups are different, making it a chiral centre. In 1-chloropropane and 1-chlorobutane, the chlorine-bearing carbon is a -CH2Cl type with two H atoms, so no chirality. In 2-chloropropane, the central carbon has two identical CH3 groups, so it is also not chiral. Hence (D) is correct.
questions.topic: Chirality and Stereoisomerism

questions.text: CH3CH2OH को CH3CHO में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है :
questions.text_english: CH3CH2OH can be converted to CH3CHO by :
questions.solution: PCC (Pyridinium chlorochromate) is a mild oxidising agent that selectively oxidises primary alcohols to aldehydes without further oxidising them to carboxylic acids. So CH3CH2OH is oxidised by PCC to CH3CHO (acetaldehyde). Catalytic hydrogenation (A) is a reduction process, not applicable here. LiAlH4 (B) is a reducing agent and would reduce aldehydes back to alcohols. KMnO4 (D) is a strong oxidising agent that would oxidise the primary alcohol all the way to the carboxylic acid (CH3COOH), not stop at the aldehyde stage. Hence (C) is correct.
questions.topic: Preparation of Aldehydes

questions.text: CH3–CH2–N(CH3)–CH2–CH2–CH3 का IUPAC नाम है :
questions.text_english: The IUPAC name for CH3–CH2–N(CH3)–CH2–CH2–CH3 is :
questions.solution: The nitrogen in the compound CH3–CH2–N(CH3)–CH2–CH2–CH3 has three substituents: one methyl group (CH3), one ethyl group (CH2CH3), and one propyl chain (CH2CH2CH3). The longest carbon chain attached to nitrogen is the propyl chain (3 carbons), so the parent amine is propan-1-amine. The other two groups on nitrogen are named as substituents: N-ethyl and N-methyl. Hence the IUPAC name is N-ethyl-N-methylpropan-1-amine, option (B).
questions.topic: IUPAC Nomenclature of Amines

questions.text: अभिकारक की सांद्रता [R] और समय 't' के मध्य आलेख नीचे दर्शाया गया है। यह आलेख दी गई अभिक्रिया की कोटि में से किसको इंगित करता है ?
questions.text_english: A plot between concentration of reactant [R] and time 't' is shown below. Which of the given order of reaction is indicated by the graph ?
questions.solution: For a zero order reaction, the rate law is: Rate = k (constant), which gives [R] = [R]0 - kt. This means the concentration of the reactant decreases linearly with time, producing a straight line with a negative slope (-k) when [R] is plotted against time t. The graph shown is a straight line with negative slope, which perfectly matches the integrated rate law for a zero order reaction. Hence the answer is (D) Zero order.
questions.topic: Order of Reaction and Integrated Rate Laws

questions.text: एथिल ब्रोमाइड, ऐल्कोहॉली सिल्वर नाइट्राइट के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है :
questions.text_english: The treatment of ethyl bromide with alcoholic silver nitrite gives :
questions.solution: When ethyl bromide reacts with alcoholic silver nitrite (AgNO2), the nitrite ion acts as an ambident nucleophile — it can bond through either the nitrogen or the oxygen. With AgNO2, the nitrogen end attacks the carbon, forming nitroethane (CH3CH2NO2), a nitro compound. This is because Ag+ helps ionise the C–Br bond forming a carbocation, and the free nitrite ion bonds through the more electronegative nitrogen end to give the C–N bond product (nitroalkane). Note that sodium nitrite (NaNO2) gives the O-bonded product (alkyl nitrite). Hence (B) is correct.
questions.topic: Reactions of Haloalkanes — Ambident Nucleophiles

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जलीय विलयनों में से किसका हिमांक उच्चतम होगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following aqueous solutions will have the highest freezing point ?
questions.solution: The depression in freezing point is given by ΔTf = i × Kf × m, where i is the van't Hoff factor (number of particles produced per formula unit). Greater the value of i, greater the depression in freezing point, and hence lower the freezing point. KCl gives 2 ions (i=2), Na2SO4 gives 3 ions (i=3), AlCl3 gives 4 ions (i=4), while glucose (a non-electrolyte) gives i=1. Since 1.0 M glucose has the smallest number of solute particles, it produces the least depression in freezing point and therefore has the highest (least depressed) freezing point among all the given options. Hence (C) is correct.
questions.topic: Colligative Properties — Depression in Freezing Point

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा ऐल्डिहाइड कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया देगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following aldehydes will undergo Cannizzaro reaction ?
questions.solution: Cannizzaro reaction is undergone by aldehydes that do not have an alpha hydrogen atom (no H on the carbon adjacent to the CHO group). In such aldehydes, concentrated NaOH causes a disproportionation — one molecule is oxidised to a carboxylate salt and another is reduced to an alcohol. Among the given options, (CH3)3C–CHO (pivaldehyde or 2,2-dimethylpropanal) has no alpha hydrogen because the carbon adjacent to CHO carries three methyl groups and no H. Options A, C, and D all have at least one alpha hydrogen, so they undergo aldol condensation instead of Cannizzaro reaction. Hence (B) is correct.
questions.topic: Cannizzaro Reaction

questions.text: निम्नलिखित समूहों में से किसके दोनों आयन जलीय विलयन में रंगीन हैं ? I. Cu+ II. Ti4+ III. Co2+ IV. Fe2+ [परमाणु क्रमांक : Cu = 29, Ti = 22, Co = 27, Fe = 26]
questions.text_english: In which of the following groups are both ions coloured in aqueous solution ? I. Cu+ II. Ti4+ III. Co2+ IV. Fe2+ [Atomic number : Cu = 29, Ti = 22, Co = 27, Fe = 26]
questions.solution: Coloured ions in transition metal compounds arise due to d-d transitions, which require partially filled d-orbitals. Cu+ has configuration [Ar] 3d10 (completely filled d), so it is colourless. Ti4+ has configuration [Ar] 3d0 (empty d), so it is also colourless. Co2+ has configuration [Ar] 3d7 (partially filled), so it is coloured (pink in aqueous solution). Fe2+ has configuration [Ar] 3d6 (partially filled), so it is also coloured (pale green in aqueous solution). Therefore group III (Co2+) and IV (Fe2+) both have coloured ions in aqueous solution. The answer is (C).
questions.topic: Colour of Transition Metal Ions

questions.text: CH3CH2CHO और CH3CH2COOH के मध्य किसके द्वारा विभेद किया जा सकता है ?
questions.text_english: CH3CH2CHO and CH3CH2COOH can be distinguished by :
questions.solution: The sodium bicarbonate test distinguishes aldehydes from carboxylic acids. Carboxylic acids (CH3CH2COOH) react with NaHCO3 to produce brisk effervescence of CO2 gas, whereas aldehydes (CH3CH2CHO) do not react with NaHCO3 and hence give no effervescence. Hinsberg test (B) is used to distinguish primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. Iodoform test (C) is used for methyl ketones and certain alcohols. Lucas test (D) distinguishes primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols. Hence (A) is the correct answer.
questions.topic: Chemical Tests to Distinguish Functional Groups

questions.text: स्तंभ I में दिए गए सेल के प्रकार को स्तंभ II में दिए गए उनके उपयोग से मिलान कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Match the type of cell given in Column I with their use given in Column II.
questions.image_description: A matching table. Column I: i. Lead storage cell, ii. Mercury cell, iii. Dry cell, iv. Fuel cell. Column II: a. Wall clock, b. Apollo Space Programme, c. Wrist watch, d. Inverter.
questions.solution: The correct matching is: Lead storage cell (i) is used in inverters and car batteries — matched with d (Inverter). Mercury cell (ii) provides a constant voltage of 1.35V and is used in wrist watches — matched with c (Wrist watch). Dry cell (iii) is the common Leclanche cell used in wall clocks — matched with a (Wall clock). Fuel cell (iv) converts chemical energy of hydrogen and oxygen directly into electricity and was famously used in the Apollo Space Programme — matched with b (Apollo Space Programme). So the correct option is (B): i-d, ii-c, iii-a, iv-b.
questions.topic: Types of Cells and Their Applications

questions.text: रसायन प्रयोगशाला में गुणात्मक विश्लेषण करते समय अभिषेक ने एक परखनली में पीले रंग का पोटैशियम क्रोमेट विलयन डाला। वह यह देखकर अचम्भित हो गया कि विलयन का रंग तुरंत नारंगी रंग में बदल गया। उसे यह अनुभूति हुई कि परखनली साफ नहीं थी अपितु उसमें किसी अन्य द्रव की कुछ बूँदें थीं। निम्नलिखित पदार्थों में से परखनली में पोटैशियम क्रोमेट विलयन डालने से पहले कौन-सा सर्वाधिक संभावित द्रव उपस्थित था ?
questions.text_english: While doing qualitative analysis in chemistry lab, Abhishek added yellow coloured potassium chromate solution into a test tube. He was surprised to see the colour of the solution changing immediately to orange. He realised that the test tube was not clean and contained a few drops of some liquid. Which of the following substances will be the most likely liquid to be present in the test tube before adding potassium chromate solution ?
questions.solution: Potassium chromate (K2CrO4) is yellow in alkaline or neutral medium. In acidic medium, chromate (CrO4^2-) is converted to dichromate (Cr2O7^2-), which is orange. The reaction is: 2CrO4^2- + 2H+ → Cr2O7^2- + H2O. An acid present in the test tube would immediately lower the pH, converting yellow chromate to orange dichromate. Among the options, HCl solution (D) is the only acid that would cause this colour change. NaHCO3 and NaOH are alkaline, and methyl orange would not cause this transformation. Hence (D) is correct.
questions.topic: Chromate-Dichromate Equilibrium

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : आयनिक विलयन के प्रतिरोध को मापने के लिए AC स्रोत का उपयोग किया जाता है। कारण (R) : यदि DC स्रोत का उपयोग किया जाता है तो आयनिक विलयन की सांद्रता बदल जाएगी।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : For measuring resistance of an ionic solution an AC source is used. Reason (R) : Concentration of ionic solution will change if DC source is used.
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D)

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. If a DC source were used to measure the resistance of an ionic solution, electrolysis would occur — ions would migrate to the electrodes and get discharged, changing the composition and concentration of the solution. This would also result in polarisation effects that give inaccurate readings. AC source is therefore used so that the direction of current reverses rapidly, preventing electrode reactions and keeping the ionic concentration constant. Hence the Reason (R) is indeed the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). Answer is (A).
questions.topic: Measurement of Conductivity

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : ताप में वृद्धि के साथ हेनरी नियम स्थिरांक (KH) घटता है। कारण (R) : जैसे-जैसे ताप बढ़ता है, द्रवों में गैसों की विलेयता घटती है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : Henry's law constant (KH) decreases with increase in temperature. Reason (R) : As the temperature increases, solubility of gases in liquids decreases.
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D)

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Henry's law states that p = KH × x, where p is the partial pressure and x is the mole fraction of the dissolved gas. As temperature increases, the solubility of gases in liquids decreases (Reason R is true). Since p = KH × x, a decrease in x at the same pressure p means KH must increase, not decrease. Therefore the Assertion (A) is false — KH actually increases with increase in temperature. The Reason (R) is true (solubility of gases decreases with temperature) but the Assertion based on it is incorrectly stated. Hence the correct answer is (D).
questions.topic: Henry's Law

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : जैसे-जैसे ऐल्किल समूह का आकार बढ़ता है, ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों की जल में घुलनशीलता घटती जाती है। कारण (R) : ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों में द्विध्रुव-द्विध्रुव अन्योन्यक्रियाएँ होती हैं।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : The solubility of aldehydes and ketones in water decreases with increase in size of the alkyl group. Reason (R) : Aldehydes and ketones have dipole-dipole interaction.
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D)

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the Assertion and the Reason are individually true. Aldehydes and ketones are soluble in water due to hydrogen bonding between the C=O group and water molecules. As the size of the alkyl group increases, the nonpolar hydrocarbon part dominates and the relative contribution of the polar C=O group decreases, reducing solubility in water — so Assertion (A) is true. Aldehydes and ketones do exhibit dipole-dipole interactions among themselves due to the polar C=O bond — so Reason (R) is also true. However, the decrease in water solubility with increasing alkyl group size is explained by the increasing hydrophobic character of the alkyl chain, not by the dipole-dipole interactions among aldehyde/ketone molecules. So (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). Answer is (B).
questions.topic: Physical Properties of Aldehydes and Ketones

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : ऐल्किल हैलाइडों के क्वथनांकों के घटने का क्रम RI > RBr > RCl > RF है। कारण (R) : वान्डरवाल्स बलों के आकर्षण के घटने का क्रम RI > RBr > RCl > RF है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : The boiling points of alkyl halides decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF. Reason (R) : The van der Waals forces of attraction decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D)

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The boiling points of alkyl halides follow the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF. This is because larger and heavier halogen atoms are more polarisable, leading to stronger van der Waals (London dispersion) forces. As the size of the halogen increases going from F to I, the van der Waals forces of attraction increase: RI > RBr > RCl > RF. Greater van der Waals forces mean more energy is needed to separate molecules, hence higher boiling points. The Reason is indeed the correct explanation of the Assertion. Answer is (A).
questions.topic: Physical Properties — Boiling Points of Alkyl Halides

questions.text: (क) CaCl2 (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 111 g mol–1) के 3 g को 260 g जल में घोलने पर बनने वाले विलयन के क्वथनांक का उन्नयन, यह मानते हुए कि CaCl2 पूर्णतया वियोजित हो गया है, परिकलित कीजिए। (जल के लिए Kb = 0.52 K kg mol–1)
questions.text_english:
(a) Calculate the elevation of boiling point of a solution when 3 g of CaCl2 (Molar mass = 111 g mol–1) was dissolved in 260 g of water, assuming that CaCl2 undergoes complete dissociation. (Kb for water = 0.52 K kg mol–1)

OR

(b) Liquids 'X' and 'Y' form an ideal solution. The vapour pressure of pure 'X' and pure 'Y' are 120 mm Hg and 160 mm Hg respectively. Calculate the vapour pressure of the solution containing equal moles of 'X' and 'Y'.
questions.instruction_line: अथवा — 'X' और 'Y' द्रव आदर्श विलयन बनाते हैं। शुद्ध 'X' और शुद्ध 'Y' के वाष्प दाब क्रमश: 120 mm Hg और 160 mm Hg हैं। 'X' और 'Y' के समान मोलों को मिलाकर बनने वाले विलयन का वाष्प दाब परिकलित कीजिए।

key_points: For part (a): Moles of CaCl2 = 3/111 = 0.027 mol. CaCl2 dissociates as CaCl2 → Ca2+ + 2Cl–, giving i = 3. Mass of solvent = 260 g = 0.260 kg. ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 3 × 0.52 × (0.027/0.260) = 3 × 0.52 × 0.1038 = 0.162 K
For part (b): Equal moles means mole fraction of X = mole fraction of Y = 0.5. P_solution = P°X × xX + P°Y × xY = 120 × 0.5 + 160 × 0.5 = 60 + 80 = 140 mm Hg

questions.solution:
Part (a): Moles of CaCl2 = 3 g ÷ 111 g mol–1 = 0.027 mol. CaCl2 dissociates completely as: CaCl2 → Ca2+ + 2Cl–, producing 3 ions per formula unit, so i = 3. Molality of solution = 0.027 mol ÷ 0.260 kg = 0.1038 mol kg–1. ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 3 × 0.52 × 0.1038 = 0.162 K. The elevation in boiling point is 0.162 K.

Part (b): Since equal moles of X and Y are mixed, mole fraction of X (xX) = 0.5 and mole fraction of Y (xY) = 0.5. By Raoult's law for ideal solutions: P_total = P°X × xX + P°Y × xY = 120 × 0.5 + 160 × 0.5 = 60 + 80 = 140 mm Hg.
questions.topic: Colligative Properties — Elevation of Boiling Point and Raoult's Law

questions.text: ऊपर दिए गए आँकड़ों के आधार पर, सांद्रता के साथ चालकता और मोलर चालकता में परिवर्तन के लिए संभावित कारण दीजिए।
questions.text_english: Based on the data given above, give plausible reason for the variation of conductivity and molar conductivity with concentration.
questions.instruction_line_english: Data table provided: Concentration 1.000, 0.100, 0.010 mol/L; Conductivity 0.1113, 0.0129, 0.00141 S cm–1; Molar conductivity 111.3, 129.0, 141.0 S cm2 mol–1

key_points: Conductivity decreases with dilution because the number of ions per unit volume (ionic concentration) decreases.
Molar conductivity increases with dilution because interionic attractions decrease, allowing ions to move more freely and conduct electricity more effectively per mole.

questions.solution: From the data, as the concentration of KCl solution decreases from 1.000 M to 0.010 M, the conductivity decreases from 0.1113 to 0.00141 S cm–1. This is because conductivity depends on the total number of ions present per unit volume. As dilution increases, the number of ions per unit volume decreases, resulting in lower conductivity. On the other hand, molar conductivity increases from 111.3 to 141.0 S cm2 mol–1 upon dilution. This is because at higher concentrations, interionic attractions (between oppositely charged ions) are stronger, which reduces the mobility of ions. Upon dilution, these interionic forces decrease, the ions become freer to move, and each mole of electrolyte contributes more to the conduction. Hence molar conductivity increases with dilution.
questions.topic: Conductivity and Molar Conductivity

questions.text: (क) अभिक्रिया 2HI → H2 + I2 के लिए वेग नियम व्यंजक लिखिए, यदि यह अभिक्रिया शून्य कोटि की है। (ख) अभिक्रिया वेग पर ताप का क्या प्रभाव होता है ? इसके लिए गणितीय व्यंजक लिखिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Write the rate law expression for the reaction 2HI → H2 + I2, if the order of the reaction is zero. (b) What is the effect of temperature on the rate of reaction ? Write a mathematical expression for the same.

key_points: Part (a): Rate = k [HI]^0 = k (constant). The rate is independent of the concentration of HI.

Part (b): Rate increases with increase in temperature. Mathematical expression: k = A × e^(–Ea/RT) (Arrhenius equation). As T increases, e^(–Ea/RT) increases, so k increases, and hence rate increases.

questions.solution:
Part (a): For the reaction 2HI → H2 + I2, if the order is zero, the rate law expression is: Rate = k[HI]^0 = k. This means the rate of reaction is constant and independent of the concentration of HI at all times.

Part (b): As temperature increases, the rate of a reaction increases. For approximately every 10°C rise in temperature, the rate of reaction approximately doubles. The mathematical expression is the Arrhenius equation: k = A × e^(–Ea/RT), where k is the rate constant, A is the pre-exponential (frequency) factor, Ea is the activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is the absolute temperature. As T increases, the exponential term increases, so k and consequently the rate of reaction increase.
questions.topic: Zero Order Reaction and Arrhenius Equation

questions.text: एथीन की अम्ल उत्प्रेरित जलयोजन की क्रियाविधि समझाइए।
questions.text_english: Explain the mechanism of acid catalysed hydration of ethene.

key_points: Step 1: Protonation — A proton (H+) from the acid adds to the double bond of ethene (electrophilic addition) to form a carbocation (ethyl carbocation, CH3CH2+).
Step 2: Nucleophilic attack — A water molecule (nucleophile) attacks the carbocation to form an oxonium ion.
Step 3: Deprotonation — The oxonium ion loses a proton to another water molecule to give ethanol (CH3CH2OH).

questions.solution: The acid-catalysed hydration of ethene proceeds by an electrophilic addition mechanism in three steps. In Step 1, a proton (H+) from the acid catalyst adds to one carbon of the C=C double bond of ethene, following Markovnikov's rule, to form an ethyl carbocation: CH2=CH2 + H+ → CH3CH2+. In Step 2, a water molecule acts as a nucleophile and attacks the positively charged carbon of the carbocation to form a protonated alcohol (oxonium ion): CH3CH2+ + H2O → CH3CH2–OH2+. In Step 3, this oxonium ion loses a proton to another water molecule (or the conjugate base of the acid), regenerating the acid catalyst and giving the product ethanol: CH3CH2OH2+ + H2O → CH3CH2OH + H3O+.
questions.topic: Preparation of Alcohols — Acid Catalysed Hydration

questions.text: (क) ऐसीटिल क्लोराइड से ऐसीटैल्डिहाइड का विरचन कैसे किया जा सकता है ? (ख) प्रोपेनोन की अपेक्षा प्रोपेनैल नाभिकरागी योगज अभिक्रियाओं के प्रति अधिक अभिक्रियाशील है। कारण दीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) How can acetaldehyde be prepared from acetyl chloride ? (b) Propanal is more reactive than propanone towards nucleophilic addition reaction. Give reason.

key_points: Part (a): Acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) is reduced using H2 in the presence of Pd/BaSO4 catalyst (Rosenmund reduction) to give acetaldehyde (CH3CHO). CH3COCl + H2 → CH3CHO + HCl.

Part (b): Propanal (an aldehyde) has one H and one CH3CH2 group on the carbonyl carbon, while propanone (a ketone) has two alkyl groups. The two alkyl groups in propanone create more steric hindrance and also donate electrons to the carbonyl carbon by inductive effect, reducing the partial positive charge on carbon and making it less susceptible to nucleophilic attack. Hence propanal is more reactive.

questions.solution:
Part (a): Acetaldehyde can be prepared from acetyl chloride by Rosenmund reduction. Acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) is reduced with hydrogen gas in the presence of palladium catalyst poisoned with barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO4). The reaction is: CH3COCl + H2 → (Pd/BaSO4) → CH3CHO + HCl. The poisoned catalyst prevents over-reduction of the aldehyde to alcohol.

Part (b): Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) is more reactive than propanone (CH3COCH3) towards nucleophilic addition reactions for two reasons. First, in propanone, two alkyl groups are attached to the carbonyl carbon, whereas in propanal only one alkyl group is present. The two alkyl groups in propanone donate electrons to the carbonyl carbon by inductive effect, reducing its partial positive charge (δ+) and making it less electrophilic. Second, two alkyl groups in propanone create greater steric hindrance around the carbonyl carbon, making it more difficult for the nucleophile to approach. Therefore, propanal reacts more readily with nucleophiles.
questions.topic: Preparation and Reactivity of Aldehydes

questions.text: (क) श्वेता ने दो द्रवों A और B के प्रत्येक के 10 mL को परस्पर मिलाया। मिलाने पर विलयन का आयतन 20.2 mL पाया गया।
questions.text_english:
(a) Shweta mixed two liquids A and B of 10 mL each. After mixing, the volume of the solution was found to be 20.2 mL.
(i) Why was there a volume change after mixing the liquids ?
(ii) Will there be an increase or decrease of temperature after mixing ?
(iii) Give one example for this type of solution.

OR

(b) (i) How does sprinkling of salt help in clearing the snow covered roads in hilly areas ?
(ii) What happens when red blood cells are kept in 0.5% (mass/vol) NaCl solution ? Justify your answer.
(iii) Write an application of reverse osmosis.
questions.instruction_line: (i) द्रवों को मिलाने पर आयतन में परिवर्तन क्यों हुआ ? (ii) मिलाने पर ताप बढ़ेगा या घटेगा ? (iii) इस प्रकार के विलयन का एक उदाहरण दीजिए। अथवा (ख) (i) पहाड़ी इलाकों में बर्फ से ढकी सड़कों को साफ करने में नमक छिड़कने से किस तरह मदद मिलती है ? (ii) क्या होता है जब लाल रुधिर कोशिकाओं को 0.5% (द्रव्यमान/आयतन) सोडियम क्लोराइड विलयन में रखा जाता है ? (iii) प्रतिलोम परासरण का एक अनुप्रयोग लिखिए।

key_points: Part (a)(i): Volume increased from 20 mL to 20.2 mL — positive deviation from Raoult's law. A-B interactions are weaker than A-A and B-B interactions. This means the molecules occupy more space (volumes are not perfectly additive).
Part (a)(ii): Temperature will decrease — mixing is endothermic (ΔHmix > 0) as energy is absorbed to break stronger A-A and B-B interactions.
Part (a)(iii): Acetone and carbon disulphide (or ethanol and cyclohexane) — example of positive deviation solution.
Part (b)(i): Salt lowers the freezing point of water due to depression of freezing point (colligative property), melting the snow at sub-zero temperatures.

Part (b)(ii): 0.5% NaCl is hypotonic compared to RBC contents (which is ~0.9%). Water enters RBCs by osmosis, causing them to swell (plasmolysis). At 0.5%, they may show some swelling but not burst like in pure water.
Part (b)(iii): Reverse osmosis is used to purify seawater/brackish water for obtaining drinking water (desalination).

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): The total volume of the solution (20.2 mL) is greater than the sum of individual volumes (10 + 10 = 20 mL). This happens because liquid A and liquid B form a non-ideal solution showing positive deviation from Raoult's law. In this case, the A-B intermolecular interactions are weaker than the A-A and B-B interactions in the pure liquids. As a result, the molecules are held less tightly and occupy slightly more space, leading to a volume increase on mixing.

Part (a)(ii): Since this is a positive deviation solution, the mixing process is endothermic (ΔHmix > 0). Energy is absorbed to overcome the stronger A-A and B-B interactions and replace them with weaker A-B interactions. Therefore, temperature will decrease after mixing.

Part (a)(iii): A mixture of acetone and carbon disulphide is a classical example of this type of solution (positive deviation from Raoult's law).

Part (b)(i): When salt is sprinkled on snow-covered roads, it dissolves in the thin film of water present on the snow surface and lowers its freezing point due to depression of freezing point (a colligative property). This causes the snow and ice to melt at a temperature below 0°C, helping to clear the roads.

Part (b)(ii): The normal saline concentration of RBCs is approximately 0.9% NaCl. A 0.5% NaCl solution is hypotonic relative to the RBC contents. When RBCs are placed in this solution, water enters the cells by osmosis (moving from a region of lower solute concentration — the surrounding solution — to higher solute concentration inside the cell). The cells swell up and may eventually burst (haemolysis).

Part (b)(iii): Reverse osmosis is widely used in the desalination of sea water to obtain pure drinking water. High pressure is applied to force sea water through a semi-permeable membrane, allowing only water molecules to pass through while retaining salts and impurities.
questions.topic: Non-ideal Solutions, Colligative Properties, Osmosis, Reverse Osmosis

questions.text: अभिक्रिया A + B → उत्पाद के लिए, अभिकारकों की विभिन्न प्रारंभिक सांद्रताओं के लिए निम्नलिखित प्रारंभिक वेग प्राप्त हुए : (तालिका दी गई है) A और B के सापेक्ष अभिक्रिया की कोटि और अभिक्रिया की समग्र कोटि ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: For the reaction A + B → Products, the following initial rates were obtained at various initial concentrations of reactants: [Table: Sl. No. 1: [A]=0.1, [B]=0.1, rate=0.05; Sl. No. 2: [A]=0.2, [B]=0.1, rate=0.10; Sl. No. 3: [A]=0.1, [B]=0.2, rate=0.05] Determine the order of the reaction with respect to A and B and overall order of the reaction.

key_points: Order with respect to A = 1 (first order). From experiments 1 and 2, doubling [A] doubles the rate.
Order with respect to B = 0 (zero order). From experiments 1 and 3, doubling [B] has no effect on rate.
Overall order = 1 + 0 = 1 (first order overall).

questions.solution: Let the rate law be: Rate = k[A]^m [B]^n. Comparing experiments 1 and 2 (where [B] is constant at 0.1 mol L–1): Rate2/Rate1 = k(0.2)^m(0.1)^n / k(0.1)^m(0.1)^n = (0.2/0.1)^m = 2^m. So 0.10/0.05 = 2 = 2^m, which gives m = 1. The reaction is first order with respect to A. Comparing experiments 1 and 3 (where [A] is constant at 0.1 mol L–1): Rate3/Rate1 = k(0.1)^m(0.2)^n / k(0.1)^m(0.1)^n = (0.2/0.1)^n = 2^n. So 0.05/0.05 = 1 = 2^n, which gives n = 0. The reaction is zero order with respect to B. Therefore, the overall order of the reaction = m + n = 1 + 0 = 1. The rate law is: Rate = k[A].
questions.topic: Order of Reaction — Determination from Experimental Data

questions.text: (क) क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र विपाटन ऊर्जा से क्या अभिप्राय है ? d4 आयन के लिए, विन्यास लिखिए यदि (i) Δo < P, तथा (ii) Δo > P है। (ख) व्याख्या कीजिए क्यों चतुष्फलकीय उपसहसंयोजन सत्ताओं में, निम्न प्रचक्रण विन्यास विरले ही देखा जाता है।
questions.text_english: (a) What is meant by crystal field splitting energy ? For a d4 ion, write the configuration if (i) Δo < P, and (ii) Δo > P. (b) Explain why in tetrahedral coordination entities, low spin configurations are rarely observed.

key_points: Crystal field splitting energy (Δo) is the energy difference between t2g and eg orbitals in an octahedral complex due to the electrostatic field of ligands.
For d4: (i) Δo < P (weak field/high spin): t2g3 eg1 — one electron goes to eg rather than pairing in t2g.
For d4: (ii) Δo > P (strong field/low spin): t2g4 eg0 — all four electrons occupy t2g orbitals with pairing.
Tetrahedral splitting energy Δt ≈ 4/9 Δo, which is much smaller than pairing energy P, so high-spin configurations are almost always favoured in tetrahedral complexes.

questions.solution:
Part (a): Crystal field splitting energy (Δo) is the energy difference between the higher energy eg set (dx2-y2 and dz2) and the lower energy t2g set (dxy, dyz, dxz) of d-orbitals in an octahedral crystal field, caused by the electrostatic repulsion from the surrounding ligands. For a d4 ion: (i) When Δo < P (pairing energy), the energy required to pair electrons exceeds the splitting energy, so the fourth electron enters the eg orbital rather than pairing in t2g. The high-spin configuration is t2g3 eg1. (ii) When Δo > P, it is energetically favourable to pair the electron in the t2g level, giving the low-spin configuration t2g4 eg0.

Part (b): In tetrahedral complexes, the crystal field splitting energy is given by Δt = (4/9)Δo, which is only about 44% of the octahedral splitting energy. Since Δt is much smaller than the pairing energy (P) in almost all cases, it is never energetically favourable for electrons to pair in the lower t2 set rather than occupy the higher e set. As a result, all tetrahedral complexes have a high-spin configuration and low-spin configurations are rarely, if ever, observed.
questions.topic: Crystal Field Theory — Splitting Energy and Spin Configuration

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए : (क) मेथिल क्लोराइड की अपेक्षा क्लोरोबेन्जीन में C–Cl आबन्ध लंबाई छोटी होती है। (ख) ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मकों का विरचन निर्जलीय अवस्थाओं में करना चाहिए। (ग) ध्रुवण घूर्णक ऐल्किल हैलाइडों के लिए, SN1 अभिक्रियाएँ रेसिमीकरण के साथ सम्पन्न होती हैं।
questions.text_english: Account for the following : (a) The C–Cl bond length in chlorobenzene is shorter than that in methyl chloride. (b) Grignard reagents should be prepared under anhydrous conditions. (c) In case of optically active alkyl halides, SN1 reactions are accompanied by racemisation.

key_points: (a) In chlorobenzene, the lone pair of Cl overlaps with the pi system of the benzene ring (resonance), giving partial C=Cl double bond character, which shortens the C-Cl bond.
(b) Grignard reagents (RMgX) react readily with water to give an alkane and Mg(OH)X, destroying the reagent. So anhydrous conditions are essential.

(c) In SN1, the carbocation intermediate is planar (sp2 hybridised). The nucleophile can attack from either face with equal probability, giving 50% retention and 50% inversion, resulting in a racemic mixture.

questions.solution:
Part (a): In chlorobenzene, the chlorine atom is directly attached to the benzene ring. The lone pairs on chlorine undergo resonance (conjugation) with the pi electrons of the ring, giving the C–Cl bond some double bond character. This partial double bond character makes the C–Cl bond shorter in chlorobenzene (approximately 169 pm) compared to methyl chloride where the C–Cl bond is a pure single bond (approximately 178 pm).

Part (b): Grignard reagents (RMgX) are extremely reactive organomagnesium compounds. If water is present, the Grignard reagent immediately reacts with water to produce an alkane and magnesium hydroxy halide: RMgX + H2O → RH + Mg(OH)X. This destroys the reagent before it can be used. Therefore, Grignard reagents must always be prepared and used under strictly anhydrous (moisture-free) conditions, using dry ether as solvent.

Part (c): In an SN1 reaction, the rate-determining step involves ionisation of the alkyl halide to form a planar carbocation intermediate, which is sp2 hybridised. Because the carbocation is planar, the nucleophile (e.g., water or another nucleophile) can attack with equal probability from either the front face or the back face of the planar intermediate. This results in 50% retention and 50% inversion of configuration, yielding an equal mixture of both enantiomers (a racemic mixture), and hence optical activity is lost.
questions.topic: Properties of C–Cl Bond, Grignard Reagents, SN1 Mechanism

questions.text: (क) निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनकी अम्लीय सामर्थ्य के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए : 3,5-डाइनाइट्रोफीनॉल, 4-मेथिलफीनॉल, फीनॉल, 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोफीनॉल (ख) क्या होता है जब : (समीकरण लिखिए) (i) फीनॉल को यशदरज के साथ आसुत किया जाता है ? (ii) ऐनिसोल को HBr के साथ अभिक्रियित किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: (a) Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their acidic strength : 3,5-dinitrophenol, 4-methylphenol, phenol, 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (b) What happens when : (write equations) (i) Phenol is distilled with Zn dust ? (ii) Anisole is treated with HBr ?

key_points: Increasing acidic strength order: 4-methylphenol < phenol < 3,5-dinitrophenol < 2,4,6-trinitrophenol. Electron-donating groups (CH3) decrease acidity; electron-withdrawing groups (NO2) increase acidity.
(b)(i) Phenol + Zn dust → Benzene + ZnO. Phenol is reduced to benzene.
(b)(ii) Anisole (C6H5OCH3) + HBr → Phenol (C6H5OH) + CH3Br. Cleavage of the C–O bond on the methyl side.

questions.solution:
Part (a): The acidity of phenols depends on the substituents on the ring. Electron-withdrawing groups (like –NO2) stabilise the phenoxide ion and increase acidity, while electron-donating groups (like –CH3) destabilise it and decrease acidity. The methyl group in 4-methylphenol donates electrons, making it less acidic than phenol itself. Nitro groups withdraw electrons strongly; 3,5-dinitrophenol has two nitro groups, and 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) has three nitro groups, making it the strongest acid. The increasing order of acidic strength is: 4-methylphenol < phenol < 3,5-dinitrophenol < 2,4,6-trinitrophenol.

Part (b)(i): When phenol is distilled with zinc dust, it undergoes reduction. The –OH group is replaced by –H, converting phenol to benzene. The reaction is: C6H5OH + Zn → C6H6 + ZnO.

Part (b)(ii): When anisole (methoxybenzene, C6H5–O–CH3) is treated with HBr, cleavage of the ether linkage occurs. Because methyl is a primary group, the protonated anisole undergoes SN2 attack by Br– on the methyl group, giving phenol and bromomethane. The reaction is: C6H5–O–CH3 + HBr → C6H5–OH + CH3Br.
questions.topic: Acidity of Phenols, Reactions of Phenol and Ethers

questions.text: C8H8O आण्विक सूत्र का कोई कार्बनिक यौगिक 'A' 2,4-DNP परीक्षण देता है। यह टॉलेन परीक्षण नहीं देता है, परन्तु NaOH और I2 के साथ पीला अवक्षेप 'B' देता है। प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण पर, यह C7H6O2 सूत्र वाला कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल 'C' देता है। 'A', 'B', 'C' की पहचान कीजिए और सम्मिलित अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए।
questions.text_english: An organic compound 'A' (molecular formula C8H8O) gives 2,4-DNP test. It does not give Tollen's test, but gives a yellow precipitate 'B' with NaOH and I2. On drastic oxidation, it gives a carboxylic acid 'C' with formula C7H6O2. Identify 'A', 'B', 'C' and write the reactions involved.

key_points: A gives 2,4-DNP test → A is a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone).
A does not give Tollen's test → A is a ketone (not an aldehyde).
A gives yellow precipitate (iodoform) with NaOH/I2 → A is a methyl ketone (CH3CO– group present). B = CHI3 (iodoform).
A has formula C8H8O and on oxidation gives C7H6O2 (benzoic acid). So A = acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) and C = benzoic acid (C6H5COOH).

questions.solution:
Identification: Compound A gives the 2,4-DNP test, confirming it has a carbonyl group (C=O). Since it does not give Tollen's test, A is not an aldehyde but a ketone. The yellow precipitate B formed with NaOH and I2 is iodoform (CHI3), confirming A has a CH3CO– (methyl ketone) group — this is the iodoform test. On drastic oxidation, A gives carboxylic acid C with formula C7H6O2, which is benzoic acid (C6H5COOH). This means A contains a phenyl group attached to the carbonyl. Combining all clues: A is acetophenone (C6H5COCH3, methyl phenyl ketone) with molecular formula C8H8O. B is iodoform (CHI3), and C is benzoic acid (C6H5COOH).

Reactions:
(1) Iodoform reaction: C6H5COCH3 + 3I2 + 3NaOH → C6H5COONa + CHI3 (B, yellow ppt) + 3NaI + 2H2O.
(2) Oxidation: C6H5COCH3 + [O] → (KMnO4/H+) → C6H5COOH (C, benzoic acid).
questions.topic: Identification of Carbonyl Compounds — Iodoform Test

questions.text: (क) α-ऐमीनो अम्लों से प्रोटीन बनने के लिए उत्तरदायी बंध का नाम लिखिए। (ख) DNA और RNA के बीच कोई दो अंतर लिखिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Name the type of linkage responsible for the formation of proteins from α-amino acids. (b) Write any two differences between DNA and RNA.

key_points: (a) Peptide bond (also called amide linkage) — formed between the –COOH group of one amino acid and the –NH2 group of another, with loss of water.
(b) DNA contains deoxyribose sugar; RNA contains ribose sugar.
(b) DNA contains thymine (T) as one of its bases; RNA contains uracil (U) in place of thymine.

questions.solution:
Part (a): The type of linkage responsible for the formation of proteins from α-amino acids is called the peptide bond (or peptide linkage). It is formed when the carboxyl group (–COOH) of one amino acid reacts with the amino group (–NH2) of another amino acid with the elimination of a water molecule, forming the –CO–NH– linkage. This bond is also classified as an amide bond.

Part (b): Two important differences between DNA and RNA are as follows. First, the sugar component differs — DNA contains 2'-deoxyribose (a pentose sugar lacking an –OH group at the 2' position), while RNA contains ribose (with an –OH group at the 2' position). Second, the nitrogenous bases differ — DNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine, whereas RNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and uracil. Thymine (which has a methyl group) is replaced by uracil in RNA.

questions.text: काबोहाइड्रेट पॉलिहाइड्रॉक्सी ऐल्डिहाइड अथवा कीटोन हैं जो बहुत अधिक संरचनात्मक विविधताओं को निरूपित करते हैं जिसका कारण है दिक्-स्थान में परमाणुओं की विभिन्न व्यवस्था, फलस्वरूप उनके सैकड़ों त्रिविम समावयवी बन जाते हैं। यद्यपि अधिकतर त्रिविम समावयवों के रासायनिक गुणधर्म ज्यादा भिन्न नहीं होते, लेकिन उनकी उपापचय की दर और जैविक प्रणालियों में उपयोग महत्त्वपूर्ण रूप से भिन्न होता है तथा वह काबोहाइड्रेटों के समग्र उपापचय को प्रभावित करता है। संरचनात्मक रूपभेद, जो त्रिविम आकाश में परमाणुओं की भिन्न व्यवस्था के कारण उत्पन्न होते हैं, त्रिविम समावयव कहलाते हैं। त्रिविम समावयवों की संख्या का अनुमान सैद्धांतिक रूप से 2n सूत्र का उपयोग करके लगाया जा सकता है जहाँ 'n' अणु में उपस्थित त्रिविम केन्द्र अथवा असममित (किरेल) कार्बन परमाणुओं की संख्या है। इन त्रिविम समावयवों में से कुछ संरचनाएँ, जो एक-दूसरे की दर्पण प्रतिबिंब होती हैं, प्रतिबिंब रूप (एनैन्टिओमर) कहलाती हैं।
questions.text_english: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones that represent enormous structural diversity in terms of the arrangement of atoms in space, resulting in hundreds of stereoisomers. Although the chemical properties of most stereoisomers may not be very different, their metabolic rate and utilization in biological systems is significantly different and known to influence the overall carbohydrate metabolism. Structural variants, which arise due to a different arrangement of atoms in three-dimensional space are known as stereoisomers. The number of stereoisomers can be theoretically estimated by using the formula 2n, where 'n' is the number of stereocenters or asymmetric (chiral) carbon atoms in a molecule. Out of these stereoisomers, there are some structures, which are mirror images of each other, and they are referred to as enantiomers.

sub_questions.text_english: Give chemical reactions to show the presence of an aldehydic group and straight chain in glucose.

key_points: Aldehyde group: Glucose reacts with Tollen's reagent (ammoniacal AgNO3) to give a silver mirror, and reacts with Fehling's solution to give a red precipitate of Cu2O.
Straight chain: Glucose on reaction with HI undergoes complete reduction to give n-hexane (a straight chain hexane), showing the carbon skeleton is unbranched.

sub_questions.solution: To show the presence of an aldehydic group in glucose: (1) Glucose reacts with Tollen's reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) to produce a silver mirror on the test tube wall — this confirms the presence of a –CHO group. Reaction: C6H12O6 + 2[Ag(NH3)2]+ + 2OH– → C6H12O7 (gluconic acid) + 2Ag (silver mirror) + 4NH3 + H2O. (2) Glucose also reduces Fehling's solution (CuSO4 + sodium potassium tartrate + NaOH) to give a brick-red precipitate of Cu2O — another confirmation of –CHO group. To show the straight chain (unbranched) carbon skeleton: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI undergoes complete reduction to give n-hexane (CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3). Since the product is a straight-chain hexane and not a branched isomer, this confirms that glucose has a straight (unbranched) chain of six carbon atoms.

sub_questions.text_english: Define anomers. [OR Draw the structure of β-D-Glucopyranose.]

key_points: Anomers are cyclic forms of monosaccharides (alpha and beta) that differ in configuration only at the anomeric carbon (C-1 in aldoses), which is the new chiral centre formed during ring closure.

sub_questions.solution: Anomers are a pair of diastereomers of cyclic monosaccharides that differ from each other only in the configuration at the anomeric carbon atom (C-1 for aldoses, C-2 for ketoses). The anomeric carbon is the new chiral centre created when the open-chain form of the sugar undergoes intramolecular cyclisation. For glucose, the two anomers are α-D-glucopyranose (–OH at C-1 is on the same side as C-6, i.e., axial in Haworth projection below the ring) and β-D-glucopyranose (–OH at C-1 is on the opposite side to C-6, i.e., equatorial or above the ring in Haworth projection).

sub_questions.text_english: Sucrose is known as invert sugar. Explain.

key_points: Sucrose is dextrorotatory (+66.5°). On hydrolysis it gives glucose (+52.5°) and fructose (−92°). The mixture is laevorotatory overall (net rotation is negative). This change of sign of optical rotation (from + to –) is called inversion, so sucrose is called invert sugar.

sub_questions.solution: Sucrose is called invert sugar because of the change in the sign of optical rotation that occurs upon its hydrolysis. Pure sucrose is dextrorotatory (rotates plane-polarised light to the right, [α] = +66.5°). When sucrose is hydrolysed by the enzyme invertase (or dilute acid), it breaks down into one molecule of glucose ([α] = +52.5°, dextrorotatory) and one molecule of fructose ([α] = −92°, laevorotatory). The resulting equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose is laevorotatory overall (net [α] ≈ −19.8°) because fructose has a larger negative rotation than glucose's positive rotation. Since the sign of rotation changes from positive (dextro) to negative (laevo) during hydrolysis, this process is called inversion and the product mixture is referred to as invert sugar.

questions.text: 1893 में वर्नर का उपसहसंयोजन सिद्धांत, उपसहसंयोजन संकुलों में आबंधों की व्याख्या करने के लिए पहला प्रयास था। यह स्मरणीय है कि 1897 में जे.जे. थॉमसन द्वारा इलेक्ट्रॉन की खोज तथा संयोजकता के इलेक्ट्रॉनिक सिद्धांत से पहले ही यह सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित किया गया था। वर्नर के पास कोई भी आधुनिक उपकरणी तकनीक नहीं थी और उसके सभी अध्ययन सामान्य प्रायोगिक तकनीकों द्वारा किए गए थे। वर्नर संकुलों में आबंधन की प्रकृति की व्याख्या करने में समर्थ हुआ और उसने निष्कर्ष निकाला कि संकुलों में धातु दो भिन्न प्रकार की संयोजकताएँ प्रदर्शित करती हैं: प्राथमिक और द्वितीयक। प्राथमिक संयोजकताएँ सामान्य रूप से आयननीय होती हैं जबकि द्वितीयक संयोजकताएँ अन-आयननीय होती हैं।
questions.text_english: Werner's coordination theory in 1893 was the first attempt to explain the bonding in coordination complexes. It must be remembered that this theory was put forward before the electron had been discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897, and before the electronic theory of valency. Werner did not have any of the modern instrumental techniques and all his studies were made using simple experimental techniques. Werner was able to explain the nature of bonding in complexes and he concluded that in complexes, the metal shows two different sorts of valency: primary and secondary. Primary valences are normally ionisable whereas secondary valences are non ionisable.

sub_questions.text_english: One mole of CrCl3.4H2O precipitates one mole of AgCl when treated with excess of AgNO3 solution. Write (i) the structural formula of the complex, and (ii) the secondary valency of Cr.

key_points: Only 1 mole of AgCl precipitates, meaning only 1 Cl– is ionisable (outside the coordination sphere). So structural formula is [Cr(H2O)4Cl2]Cl.
Secondary valency of Cr = coordination number = 6 (4 H2O + 2 Cl inside the coordination sphere).

sub_questions.solution: Since one mole of CrCl3.4H2O gives only one mole of AgCl with excess AgNO3, only one chloride ion is free (present outside the coordination sphere) and can be precipitated. The remaining two Cl– and all four H2O molecules are within the coordination sphere. Therefore, the structural formula of the complex is [Cr(H2O)4Cl2]Cl. The primary valency (ionisable, shown as outer sphere) = 1 (one Cl– outside). The secondary valency of Cr = coordination number = 6 (four H2O molecules and two Cl– atoms directly bonded to Cr inside the coordination sphere).

sub_questions.text_english: What is the difference between a complex and a double salt ?

key_points: A double salt dissociates completely in aqueous solution to give all its constituent ions (e.g., potash alum gives K+, Al3+, and SO4^2–). A complex salt (coordination compound) retains its complex ion intact in solution and does not dissociate completely (e.g., K4[Fe(CN)6] gives K+ and [Fe(CN)6]^4– ions, not free Fe2+ and CN– ions).

sub_questions.solution: A double salt is formed by the combination of two simple salts that, when dissolved in water, dissociate completely to give all the constituent ions as if each individual salt were dissolved separately. For example, potash alum, KAl(SO4)2.12H2O, ionises in water to give K+, Al3+, and SO4^2– ions. In contrast, a complex salt (coordination compound) contains a complex ion that remains intact even in aqueous solution and does not dissociate completely into its simple ions. For example, potassium ferrocyanide K4[Fe(CN)6] gives K+ ions and the complex [Fe(CN)6]^4– ion in solution, with no free Fe2+ or CN– ions detectable.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित संकुलों को उनके विलयन में चालकता के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए : [Cr(NH3)3Cl3], [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3, [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following complexes in the increasing order of conductivity of their solution: [Cr(NH3)3Cl3], [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3, [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 [OR Write two differences between primary and secondary valences in coordination compounds.]

key_points: Conductivity depends on the number of ions produced in solution. [Cr(NH3)3Cl3] gives 0 ions (non-electrolyte, lowest conductivity). [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 gives 3 ions (1 complex + 2 Cl–). [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3 gives 4 ions (1 complex + 3 Cl–, highest conductivity).
Increasing order: [Cr(NH3)3Cl3] < [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 < [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3.

sub_questions.solution: The electrical conductivity of a coordination compound in solution depends on the total number of ions it produces upon dissolution. [Cr(NH3)3Cl3] has no ions outside the coordination sphere; it is a non-electrolyte and produces zero free ions, giving the lowest conductivity. [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 ionises as [Cr(NH3)5Cl]2+ + 2Cl–, giving 3 total ions, so it has intermediate conductivity. [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3 ionises as [Cr(NH3)6]3+ + 3Cl–, giving 4 total ions, so it has the highest conductivity. Therefore the increasing order of conductivity is: [Cr(NH3)3Cl3] < [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 < [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3.

questions.text: (क) (i) किसी गैल्वेनी सेल के लिए, निम्नलिखित अर्ध अभिक्रियाएँ दी गई हैं। निर्णय लीजिए कि कौन-सी, अपचयन अभिक्रिया रहेगी और किसका प्रतिलोमन होकर ऑक्सीकरण अभिक्रिया होगी। अपने उत्तर के लिए कारण दीजिए। (I) Cr3+ + 3e– → Cr(s); E° = –0.74 V (II) Fe2+ + 2e– → Fe(s); E° = –0.44 V (ii) उस सेल को निरूपित कीजिए जिसमें निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया होती है : Mg(s) + 2Ag+(0.001 M) → Mg2+(0.100 M) + 2Ag(s), यदि E°cell = 3.17 V है, तो Ecell का परिकलन कीजिए। (log 10 = 1) अथवा (ख) (i) कोलराउश नियम बताइए। इसके कोई दो अनुप्रयोग दीजिए। (ii) ΛmNH4Cl, ΛmNaOH और ΛmNaCl क्रमश: 129.8, 217.4 और 108.9 S cm2 mol–1 हैं। 1×10–2 M, NH4OH विलयन की मोलर चालकता 9.33 S cm2 mol–1 है। इस सांद्रता पर NH4OH विलयन की वियोजन मात्रा (α) परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) For a galvanic cell, the following half reactions are given. Decide, which will remain as reduction reaction and which will be reversed to become an oxidation reaction. Give reason for your answer. (I) Cr3+ + 3e– → Cr(s); E° = –0.74 V (II) Fe2+ + 2e– → Fe(s); E° = –0.44 V (ii) Represent the cell in which the following reaction takes place: Mg(s) + 2Ag+(0.001 M) → Mg2+(0.100 M) + 2Ag(s). Calculate Ecell if E°cell = 3.17 V. (log 10 = 1)

OR

(b) (i) State Kohlrausch's law. Give any two applications of it. (ii) Λ°m NH4Cl, Λ°m NaOH and Λ°m NaCl are 129.8, 217.4, and 108.9 S cm2 mol–1 respectively. Molar conductivity of 1×10–2 M solution of NH4OH is 9.33 S cm2 mol–1. Calculate the degree of dissociation (α) of NH4OH solution at this concentration.

key_points: Part (a)(i): Fe2+/Fe has higher (less negative) E° (–0.44 V), so Fe2+ is more easily reduced. Fe2+ + 2e– → Fe(s) is the reduction. Cr/Cr3+ is reversed (oxidation): Cr(s) → Cr3+ + 3e–.
Part (b)(i): Kohlrausch's law states that at infinite dilution, the molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the individual contributions of its cation and anion.

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): In a galvanic cell, the species with the higher (less negative or more positive) standard reduction potential undergoes reduction at the cathode, while the species with the lower standard reduction potential is reversed to undergo oxidation at the anode. Here, E°(Fe2+/Fe) = –0.44 V is higher than E°(Cr3+/Cr) = –0.74 V. Therefore, Fe2+ + 2e– → Fe(s) is the reduction half-reaction (cathode). The Cr reaction is reversed: Cr(s) → Cr3+ + 3e– is the oxidation half-reaction (anode). The reason is that the species with higher reduction potential has a greater tendency to gain electrons (be reduced).

Part (a)(ii): Cell notation: Mg(s) | Mg2+(0.100 M) || Ag+(0.001 M) | Ag(s). At the anode: Mg → Mg2+ + 2e–; at cathode: 2Ag+ + 2e– → 2Ag. n = 2. Using the Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log([Mg2+]/[Ag+]2) = 3.17 – (0.0591/2) × log(0.100/(0.001)2) = 3.17 – 0.02955 × log(0.100/10–6) = 3.17 – 0.02955 × log(105) = 3.17 – 0.02955 × 5 = 3.17 – 0.1478 ≈ 3.02 V.

Part (b)(i): Kohlrausch's law states that at infinite dilution, the molar conductivity of an electrolyte equals the sum of the limiting molar conductivities of its constituent cations and anions, each multiplied by the number of ions produced per formula unit. Mathematically: Λ°m = ν+ λ°+ + ν– λ°–. Two applications: (1) It is used to calculate the limiting molar conductivity (Λ°m) of weak electrolytes (like CH3COOH or NH4OH) which cannot be determined by direct extrapolation. (2) It is used to determine the degree of dissociation (α) and the dissociation constant of weak electrolytes.

Part (b)(ii): First, Λ°m(NH4OH) is calculated using Kohlrausch's law: Λ°m(NH4OH) = Λ°m(NH4Cl) + Λ°m(NaOH) – Λ°m(NaCl) = 129.8 + 217.4 – 108.9 = 238.3 S cm2 mol–1. The degree of dissociation is: α = Λm / Λ°m = 9.33 / 238.3 = 0.0391 ≈ 0.039. Therefore, approximately 3.9% of NH4OH is dissociated at this concentration.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) In a chemistry practical class, the teacher gave his students an amine 'X' having molecular formula C2H7N, and asked the students to identify the type of amine. One of the students, Neeta, observed that it reacts with C6H5SO2Cl, to give a compound which dissolves in NaOH solution. Can you help Neeta to identify the compound 'X'? (ii) Arrange the following in the increasing order of their pKb value in aqueous phase: C6H5NH2, (CH3)2NH, NH3, CH3NH2, (CH3)3N (iii) Aniline on nitration gives considerable amount of meta product along with ortho and para products. Why? (iv) Convert aniline to: (I) p-bromoaniline (II) phenol

OR

(b) (i) Arun heated a mixture of ethylamine and CHCl3 with ethanolic KOH, which forms a foul smelling gas. Write the chemical equation involved. (ii) Identify A and B in the following reactions [diagram showing nitrobenzene being reduced with H2/Pd/ethanol to give aniline; aniline reacting with Br2/NaOH to give B]. (iii) Convert aniline to: (I) benzene (II) sulphanilic acid

key_points: Part (a)(i): C2H7N is CH3NH2 (methylamine) or C2H5NH2 (ethylamine) or (CH3)2NH (dimethylamine). Hinsberg test: reaction with C6H5SO2Cl to give a product soluble in NaOH → primary amine (product is sulfonamide with acidic N-H, soluble in NaOH). C2H7N with primary amine character = ethylamine (C2H5NH2).
Part (a)(ii): Higher Kb means lower pKb (more basic). Order of basicity: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N > NH3 > C6H5NH2. So increasing pKb order: (CH3)2NH < CH3NH2 < (CH3)3N < NH3 < C6H5NH2.
Part (a)(iii): Aniline in strongly acidic conditions (HNO3/H2SO4) gets protonated to form anilinium ion (C6H5NH3+), which is an electron-withdrawing meta-director. Hence meta product is also formed.
Part (a)(iv)(I): Aniline → (acetylation with Ac2O) → acetanilide → (Br2/AcOH) → p-bromoacetanilide → (hydrolysis H3O+) → p-bromoaniline.
Part (a)(iv)(II): Aniline → (NaNO2/HCl, 0-5°C) → benzene diazonium chloride → (H2O/warm) → phenol.

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): Molecular formula C2H7N corresponds to ethylamine (C2H5NH2), methylamine with CH3 and NH2CH3, or dimethylamine. In the Hinsberg test, when an amine reacts with benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl): a primary amine gives a sulphonamide (–SO2NHR) which is soluble in NaOH (because the N–H is acidic). A secondary amine gives an insoluble sulphonamide. Since Neeta observed that the product dissolves in NaOH, compound X is a primary amine. The primary amine with formula C2H7N is ethylamine (C2H5NH2).

Part (a)(ii): Basicity of amines in aqueous phase follows: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N > NH3 > C6H5NH2. (Dimethylamine is the strongest base due to both inductive donation of two methyl groups and good solvation; trimethylamine is weaker than dimethylamine due to steric hindrance reducing solvation; aniline is the weakest as the lone pair on N is delocalised into the ring.) Since pKb = –log Kb, higher basicity means lower pKb. Increasing order of pKb: (CH3)2NH < CH3NH2 < (CH3)3N < NH3 < C6H5NH2.

Part (a)(iii): Aniline is normally an ortho-para director because the –NH2 group donates electrons to the ring. However, when nitration is carried out in the presence of a strong acid mixture (conc. HNO3 + conc. H2SO4), a significant portion of aniline gets protonated to form the anilinium ion (C6H5NH3+). The –NH3+ group is a strong electron-withdrawing group and is a meta-director. Hence, nitration of the anilinium ion gives the meta product. As a result, the overall nitration of aniline gives a mixture containing ortho, para (from free aniline) and meta (from anilinium ion) products.

Part (a)(iv)(I): Aniline cannot be directly brominated to get p-bromoaniline cleanly (it gives tribromination). To get p-bromoaniline: Step 1 — Protect the amino group by acetylation: C6H5NH2 + (CH3CO)2O → C6H5NHCOCH3 (acetanilide) + CH3COOH. Step 2 — Bromination: C6H5NHCOCH3 + Br2/AcOH → 4-BrC6H4NHCOCH3 (p-bromoacetanilide). Step 3 — Hydrolysis: 4-BrC6H4NHCOCH3 + H2O/H+ → 4-BrC6H4NH2 (p-bromoaniline) + CH3COOH.

Part (a)(iv)(II): Step 1 — Diazotisation: C6H5NH2 + NaNO2 + HCl (0–5°C) → C6H5N2+Cl– (benzene diazonium chloride). Step 2 — Hydrolysis: C6H5N2+Cl– + H2O (warm) → C6H5OH (phenol) + N2 + HCl.

Part (b)(i): Carbylamine reaction: C2H5NH2 + CHCl3 + 3KOH (alc.) → C2H5NC (ethyl isocyanide, foul-smelling) + 3KCl + 3H2O.

Part (b)(ii): A is nitrobenzene (C6H5NO2) because reduction of A with H2/Pd/ethanol gives aniline (C6H5NH2). B is obtained by treating aniline with Br2/NaOH; this is the reaction for preparation of bromobenzene via deamination — but with Br2/NaOH aniline gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline. Actually, looking at the scheme: Br2/NaOH on aniline (going backwards from aniline) suggests Hofmann bromamide degradation of an amide — but here B is the starting material of aniline via Br2/NaOH. The Hofmann degradation: RCONH2 + Br2 + 4NaOH → RNH2 + Na2CO3 + 2NaBr + 2H2O. For aniline (C6H5NH2) formed from B by Hofmann degradation: B = benzamide (C6H5CONH2). So A = nitrobenzene (C6H5NO2); B = benzamide (C6H5CONH2).

Part (b)(iii)(I): To convert aniline to benzene: C6H5NH2 + NaNO2 + HCl (0–5°C) → C6H5N2+Cl– (diazonium salt). Then: C6H5N2+Cl– + H3PO2 + H2O → C6H6 (benzene) + N2 + HCl (reduction by hypophosphorous acid).

Part (b)(iii)(II): To convert aniline to sulphanilic acid (4-aminobenzenesulphonic acid): C6H5NH2 + H2SO4 → C6H5NH3+ HSO4– (anilinium hydrogen sulphate). On heating at ~180°C (baking): rearrangement occurs to give 4-aminobenzenesulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid, H2N–C6H4–SO3H) via the process of sulphonation.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) When pyrolusite ore is fused with KOH, in presence of air, a dark green coloured product 'A' is obtained which changes to purple coloured compound 'B' in acidic medium. (I) Write the formulae of 'A' and 'B'. (II) Write the ionic equation for the reaction when compound 'B' reacts with Fe2+ in acidic medium. (ii) Give reasons: (I) Ce4+ in aqueous solution is a good oxidising agent. (II) The actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction. (III) E°Zn2+/Zn value is more negative than expected, whereas E°Cu2+/Cu is positive.

OR

(b) (i) While studying the periodic properties, Arti came across an abnormal behaviour in the atomic size of Hf. She found that, even though Hf is placed below Zr in the same group, both have almost similar atomic sizes. (I) Which phenomenon is responsible for the above behaviour? Define it. (II) Mention any other consequence of the above phenomenon. (ii) Give reasons for the following: (I) Transition metals exhibit catalytic properties. (II) Transition metals have high enthalpy of atomisation. (III) Sc is a transition element, while Zn is not.

key_points: A = K2MnO4 (potassium manganate, dark green); B = KMnO4 (potassium permanganate, purple).
Ionic equation: MnO4– + Fe2+ in acidic medium: MnO4– + 5Fe2+ + 8H+ → Mn2+ + 5Fe3+ + 4H2O.
Ce4+ is a good oxidiser because Ce4+ + e– → Ce3+; Ce3+ has stable 4f0 configuration (empty f shell), making the reduction strongly favourable.
Actinoid contraction is greater than lanthanoid contraction because 5f orbitals are less effective at shielding than 4f orbitals.
E°Zn is more negative due to high atomisation enthalpy and low hydration enthalpy of Zn2+. E°Cu is positive due to low atomisation enthalpy and high hydration enthalpy of Cu2+.

For (b)(i): Lanthanoid contraction — due to poor shielding by 4f electrons, effective nuclear charge increases across lanthanoids, shrinking atomic radii. Consequence: similar properties of elements in 5th and 6th periods of the same group.
Transition metals show catalytic properties due to variable oxidation states and ability to provide surface for reactants.
High enthalpy of atomisation due to strong metallic bonding from unpaired d-electrons.

Sc (Z=21) has electronic configuration [Ar]3d14s2. In Sc3+ the configuration is [Ar]3d0 which has an incomplete (empty) d-subshell in a lower oxidation state context. In contrast, Zn (Z=30) has [Ar]3d104s2; Zn2+ has [Ar]3d10 — a completely filled d-subshell. A transition element must have at least one ion with a partially filled d-subshell, so Zn is not a transition element.

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i)(I): When pyrolusite ore (MnO2) is fused with KOH in the presence of air, product A is potassium manganate, K2MnO4 (dark green). In acidic medium, K2MnO4 disproportionates to give product B, potassium permanganate, KMnO4 (purple/violet). Reaction: MnO2 + 2KOH + [O] → K2MnO4 + H2O. Disproportionation: 3K2MnO4 + 2H2SO4 → 2KMnO4 + MnO2 + 2K2SO4 + 2H2O. So A = K2MnO4 and B = KMnO4.

Part (a)(i)(II): In acidic medium, KMnO4 (permanganate) oxidises Fe2+ to Fe3+ while being reduced from Mn7+ to Mn2+. The ionic equation is: MnO4–(aq) + 5Fe2+(aq) + 8H+(aq) → Mn2+(aq) + 5Fe3+(aq) + 4H2O(l).

Part (a)(ii)(I): Ce4+ is a good oxidising agent in aqueous solution because on reduction it forms Ce3+, which has the electronic configuration [Xe]4f1 — actually Ce3+ is [Xe]4f1 which is relatively stable, but more importantly, Ce4+ is reduced to Ce3+, and the Ce4+/Ce3+ couple has a high positive reduction potential (+1.61 V), making Ce4+ a strong oxidising agent. The driving force is that Ce3+ corresponds to a completely empty 4f-subshell (Ce3+ is [Xe]4f0? — actually Ce3+ = [Xe]4f1, but Ce4+ = [Xe]4f0), so Ce4+ gaining an electron to achieve the stable empty 4f configuration makes the process energetically highly favourable.

Part (a)(ii)(II): The actinoid contraction (decrease in atomic/ionic radii across the actinoid series, 5f elements) is greater per element than the lanthanoid contraction (across the 4f series). This is because the 5f orbitals are more diffuse and have poorer shielding efficiency compared to 4f orbitals. Consequently, as protons are added across the actinoid series, the effective nuclear charge experienced by outer electrons increases more sharply, leading to greater contraction per element compared to lanthanoids.

Part (a)(ii)(III): The E° value of Zn2+/Zn is more negative than expected (–0.76 V, which is more negative than what periodic trends would predict for a d10 element), because zinc has a completely filled d-subshell and has a relatively high enthalpy of atomisation plus a comparatively lower hydration enthalpy for Zn2+ ion. The high energy required to atomise Zn metal is not compensated sufficiently by the hydration enthalpy, making the electrode potential more negative. On the other hand, Cu has a positive E°(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V because copper has a low enthalpy of atomisation and a relatively high hydration enthalpy of Cu2+ ion, so the overall energy balance favours the reduction of Cu2+ to Cu, giving a positive electrode potential.

Part (b)(i)(I): The phenomenon responsible is lanthanoid contraction. It is defined as the steady decrease in the size (atomic and ionic radii) of lanthanoid elements (La to Lu, Z = 57 to 71) as the atomic number increases. This contraction is caused by the poor shielding ability of 4f electrons — as each proton is added to the nucleus across the lanthanoid series, the added electrons go into 4f orbitals that do not effectively shield the outer electrons from the increasing nuclear charge, so the effective nuclear charge increases and the atomic size contracts. Because of this progressive contraction through all 14 lanthanoids, by the time the 5d series begins again (from Hf onwards), the size of Hf has shrunk to become almost identical to that of Zr in the period above.

Part (b)(i)(II): Another consequence of lanthanoid contraction is that the elements of the second and third transition series (4d and 5d elements in the same group) have almost identical atomic radii and similar physical and chemical properties. For example, Zr and Hf are extremely difficult to separate from each other because of their nearly identical sizes and properties.

Part (b)(ii)(I): Transition metals exhibit catalytic properties for two main reasons. First, they can exist in multiple oxidation states due to the availability of unfilled d-orbitals, which allows them to form intermediates with reactants at different oxidation levels, providing an alternative pathway of lower activation energy. Second, transition metals can adsorb reactants on their surfaces, bringing them close together and weakening bonds, thereby facilitating the reaction (heterogeneous catalysis).

Part (b)(ii)(II): Transition metals have high enthalpies of atomisation because they have a large number of unpaired d-electrons that contribute to strong metallic bonding (in addition to s-electrons). The more the number of unpaired electrons contributing to bonding in the metallic crystal, the stronger the metal-metal bonds, and consequently the more energy is required to atomise the metal (convert it to gaseous atoms). This results in high melting points and high enthalpies of atomisation.

Part (b)(ii)(III): A transition element is defined as an element that has at least one ion with a partially filled d-subshell. Scandium (Sc, Z = 21) has the ground state configuration [Ar]3d14s2. When it forms Sc3+ (its common ion), the configuration becomes [Ar]3d0 — the d-subshell is empty. However, in the Sc2+ or Sc1+ state (though uncommon), d-electrons are present, and by the conventional definition used in CBSE, Sc is considered a transition element because its ground state configuration includes a d-electron. Zinc (Zn, Z = 30) has the ground state configuration [Ar]3d104s2. Its common ion Zn2+ has the configuration [Ar]3d10 — a completely filled d-subshell. Since Zn and all its ions have completely filled d-orbitals, it does not qualify as a transition element by the standard definition.
